entry_state: Chapter 1 establishes why identical journals can hide different rate exposures, distinguishes a feasible interval from a probability law, and turns that distinction into a source-to-history-to-scenario workflow. The next burden is to demonstrate complete company statements and revisions rather than only one borrowing.
exit_state: Northstar now has joined historical balances, cash flows, revisions and symbolic future statements; the same debt fraction connects them. A separate parent/subsidiary case begins with supplied opening balances and narrow tax premises, ready to test interactions that isolated method examples miss.
findings: Northstar's opening balance and two half-year movement tables state currency units, homogeneous units, depreciation timing and tax simplifications. The recoverable annual flows C=245, P=155 and S=145 follow from explicit scope, while the fixed/floating split remains unidentified.

The historical statements reconcile: annual profit 29.6, operating cash 45.6, cash increase 14.6 and closing equity 90.6. The distinction between prepaid tax at June and annual cash tax is locally explained.

The revision example distinguishes published evidence from database possession and rejects mixing annual corrected revenue with an incompatible old interim total. The later corrected opening makes the forecast archival, not an investor forecast available in January.

The symbolic forecast retains one alpha across cash, profit and equity. The portable calculation explains atomic delivery, uncertain acknowledgements, exact retries and explicit missing values using the same company amounts.
The parent/subsidiary opening on page18 is readable but its section remains incomplete until subsequent cash, tax and ownership consequences are read. No confirmed defect in this segment.
